postings.text: CSQ327R219 PLEASE NOTE : Due to federal contract requirements and client site access obligations, U.S. citizenship and eligibility for a U.S. government secret clearance are required to access classified information. Candidates with an active Secret or higher clearance are strongly encouraged to apply. About Databricks At Databricks, we are passionate about enabling data teams to solve the world's toughest problems, from making the next mode of transportation a reality to accelerating the development of medical breakthroughs. We do this by building and running the world's best data and AI infrastructure platform so our customers can use deep data insights to improve their business. Founded by engineers, and customer obsessed, we leap at every opportunity to solve technical challenges, from designing next-gen UI/UX for interfacing with data to scaling our services and infrastructure across millions of virtual machines. And we're only getting started. The Role As a Sr. Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE), you will work with federal government customers to build and productionize solutions to their data & AI challenges using the Databricks platform. You will own the architecture, lead design decisions, and implement end-to-end systems spanning data engineering, AI, and application development. We work cross-functionally to shape long-term strategic priorities and initiatives alongside engineering, product, and developer relations. FDEs deliver with customer empathy, integrating with client systems, training, and other technical needs to help customers get most value out of their data. This is a hands-on, customer-facing role for builders who thrive at the intersection of technology and business impact. The ideal candidate combines engineering expertise with adaptability, curiosity, and a passion for working with customers and teammates to solve complex problems that drive measurable outcomes. FDEs are billable and know how to complete projects according to specification with exceptional customer empathy. Please note: this role is hybrid and has a requirement to travel to customer locations 20-25% of the time The impact you will have: Production Solution Delivery: Lead impactful customer technical projects by delivering production-grade systems, designing and building reference architectures, custom applications and data ingestion and ML/AI model integration Transformational Impact: Guide strategic customers as they implement transformational big data projects including end-to-end design, build and deployment of industry-leading big data and AI applications. Work with engagement managers to scope technical delivery work with input from the customer Empower Customers: Guide customers on architecture and design; bootstrap or implement customer projects which leads to a customers' successful understanding, evaluation and adoption of Databricks. Own the Architecture: Lead architecture and design decisions, ensuring solutions are secure, scalable, and aligned with both customer needs and Databricks best practices. Deliver Technical Components: Work with the Databricks technical team, Project Manager, Architect and Customer team to ensure the technical components of the engagement are delivered to meet customer's needs Cross-Collaborate: Work with Engineers and Customer Support to provide product and implementation feedback and to guide rapid resolution for engagement specific product and support issues Customer Immersion: Embed with customer teams, engaging with stakeholders from technical ICs to executives to deeply understand challenges and deliver impact. Reusable Assets & Scale: Contribute accelerators, frameworks, and best practices that scale impact across accounts and influence the Databricks product roadmap. What We're Looking For: Minimum Qualifications: 5+ years experience in data engineering, data platforms & analytics, or software engineering Fluency in writing code in Python, Scala, JavaScript/TypeScript, and modern frameworks

postings.title: Senior Application Security Engineer
postings.text: As a Senior Security Engineer within Application Security at Datadog, you will help secure emerging application architectures where established security patterns may not yet exist, including agentic applications, LLM-enabled products, protocol-driven tool use, and untrusted execution environments. You will establish and validate security models, requirements, and controls while partnering with product and platform teams to develop secure-by-default approaches. Your work will address evolving trust boundaries, agent identity, data access, tool permissions, and runtime behavior through threat modeling, security solutions, and practical implementation. You will have the opportunity to shape how Datadog safely supports new application paradigms and address emerging security risks before they become systemic. At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them. What You’ll Do: Define security models, requirements, and guardrails for emerging application architectures where established patterns are incomplete or do not yet exist. Design, implement, and validate practical security controls that reduce risk in emerging architectures and high-risk system behaviors. Shape how emerging systems authenticate, authorize actions, isolate workloads, and access data, applying least-privilege principles throughout. Partner with product, platform, Infrastructure Security, and other engineering teams to identify security gaps and embed secure-by-default requirements from early design through production. Lead threat modeling and security assessments for new and existing products, focusing on evolving threats, unfamiliar trust boundaries, and new interaction patterns. Prioritize and drive remediation of emerging security risks, including continuous security testing where it provides durable coverage, and refine security approaches as architectures and threats evolve. Who You Are: You have 5+ years of experience in software engineering or development in a collaborative environment, with Go, Rust, or Python experience preferred. You have experience in security and/or infrastructure/platform engineering, with exposure to distributed systems, application platforms, or agent-based architectures. You have designed or implemented security controls within application infrastructure, such as authentication, authorization, API security, zero-trust networking, workload protection, sandboxing, or runtime hardening. You understand common application security vulnerabilities and mitigation techniques, including those relevant to LLM applications and agentic systems; familiarity with LLM frameworks and protocols such as MCP or A2A is a plus. You bring strong problem-solving skills and can work independently and collaboratively in ambiguous or rapidly evolving problem spaces. You have successfully driven security initiatives with engineering and leadership stakeholders and are committed to staying current with security practices, emerging technologies, and evolving threats. Datadog values people from all walks of life. We know not everyone will meet all the above qualifications on day one. That’s okay. postings.title: Digital Adoption & Lifecycle Manager
postings.text: About Mixpanel Mixpanel is the leading product intelligence and analytics platform, trusted by more than 29,000 companies to help understand how people use the products they build. By combining powerful analytics with AI that knows your business, Mixpanel helps teams see what’s working, diagnose what’s not, and decide what to build next. Learn more at mixpanel.com . About the Customer Digital Experience Team Customer Digital Experience sits within Customer Engineering, the technical arm of Mixpanel's Customer organization. Our sharpest focus is the digital-only segment: thousands of companies with no proactive account coverage. Some have technical resources available to them, but that support is entirely reactive. It answers the ticket and solves the problem in front of it. Nobody is watching for the customer who implemented and then never built a report, or the account whose usage has been sliding for a month. Our job is to be proactive,, and everything we build should be as automated as possible, without a human initiating it. Our programs run across the full customer base and are not one-size-fits-all. We build flows that branch and adapt by segment, tuning the content, timing, and channel for who's receiving them. An onboarding flow for a digital-only customer carries the whole experience; the version reaching an account with a dedicated team is tuned to complement what that team is already doing. Same underlying program, deliberately different execution, continuously optimized based on what each segment responds to. We're close to the data and to the technical reality of how customers implement and use Mixpanel. We're not guessing at what customers are doing; we can see it, and we build against it. This is a small, new team standing up a new function. The playbook isn't written yet; we're writing it together. About the Role As our Digital Adoption & Lifecycle Manager, you'll own the communications that drive adoption, retention, and expansion across Mixpanel's customer base, with our digital-only customers as the sharpest test of whether the programs work. You'll design lifecycle programs triggered by real behavior: a team that just implemented but hasn't built their first report, an account whose query volume dropped for three straight weeks, a power user hitting the edge of their current plan. Then you'll write the emails and in-product messages that move them forward. This is a builder's role, not a maintainer's role. You'll define the segmentation, write the copy, set up the triggers, instrument the measurement, and then argue with the data about what to change. It's also a deeply collaborative one. You'll work hand in hand with our Customer Success Digital Programs Manager, sharing a roadmap and dividing the work. You'll partner with Marketing on the overall email calendar so our lifecycle sends and their campaigns aren't competing for the same inbox. You'll support adoption initiatives coming out of Product, turning a launch into something customers actually try. And you'll take cues from customer-facing teams about what's landing and what isn't. Very little of this job happens alone. You'll also help define what agentic customer success looks like at Mixpanel. The scaled programs we build today are rules and triggers; the ones we build next will involve AI agents that can interpret a customer's situation, decide what that customer needs, and act. We're early here and we don't have the answers. We want someone who is already experimenting, who already has opinions about where agents help and where they break trust, and who wants to shape how this gets built. If you like clean handoffs and finished systems, this isn't it. If you want to build the thing from zero and own the number it moves, read on. Responsibilities Build the lifecycle communication program end-to-end across onboarding, adoption, retention, and expansion, from strategy through copy, build, launch, and iteration Create programs that serve the full cus

postings.text: About Mixpanel Mixpanel is the leading product intelligence and analytics platform, trusted by more than 29,000 companies to help understand how people use the products they build. By combining powerful analytics with AI that knows your business, Mixpanel helps teams see what’s working, diagnose what’s not, and decide what to build next. Learn more at mixpanel.com . About the Customer Digital Experience Team Customer Digital Experience sits within Customer Engineering, the technical arm of Mixpanel's Customer organization. Our sharpest focus is the digital-only segment: thousands of companies with no proactive account coverage. Some have technical resources available to them, but that support is entirely reactive. It answers the ticket and solves the problem in front of it. Nobody is watching for the customer who implemented and then never built a report, or the account whose usage has been sliding for a month. Our job is to be proactive,, and everything we build should be as automated as possible, without a human initiating it. Our programs run across the full customer base and are not one-size-fits-all. We build flows that branch and adapt by segment, tuning the content, timing, and channel for who's receiving them. An onboarding flow for a digital-only customer carries the whole experience; the version reaching an account with a dedicated team is tuned to complement what that team is already doing. Same underlying program, deliberately different execution, continuously optimized based on what each segment responds to. We're close to the data and to the technical reality of how customers implement and use Mixpanel. We're not guessing at what customers are doing; we can see it, and we build against it. This is a small, new team standing up a new function. The playbook isn't written yet; we're writing it together. About the Role As our Digital Adoption & Lifecycle Manager, you'll own the communications that drive adoption, retention, and expansion across Mixpanel's customer base, with our digital-only customers as the sharpest test of whether the programs work. You'll design lifecycle programs triggered by real behavior: a team that just implemented but hasn't built their first report, an account whose query volume dropped for three straight weeks, a power user hitting the edge of their current plan. Then you'll write the emails and in-product messages that move them forward. This is a builder's role, not a maintainer's role. You'll define the segmentation, write the copy, set up the triggers, instrument the measurement, and then argue with the data about what to change. It's also a deeply collaborative one. You'll work hand in hand with our Customer Success Digital Programs Manager, sharing a roadmap and dividing the work. You'll partner with Marketing on the overall email calendar so our lifecycle sends and their campaigns aren't competing for the same inbox. You'll support adoption initiatives coming out of Product, turning a launch into something customers actually try. And you'll take cues from customer-facing teams about what's landing and what isn't. Very little of this job happens alone. You'll also help define what agentic customer success looks like at Mixpanel. The scaled programs we build today are rules and triggers; the ones we build next will involve AI agents that can interpret a customer's situation, decide what that customer needs, and act. We're early here and we don't have the answers. We want someone who is already experimenting, who already has opinions about where agents help and where they break trust, and who wants to shape how this gets built. If you like clean handoffs and finished systems, this isn't it. If you want to build the thing from zero and own the number it moves, read on. postings.text: About Mixpanel Mixpanel is the leading product intelligence and analytics platform, trusted by more than 29,000 companies to help understand how people use the products they build. By combining powerful analytics with AI that knows your business, Mixpanel helps teams see what’s working, diagnose what’s not, and decide what to build next. Learn more at mixpanel.com . About the Customer Digital Experience Team Customer Digital Experience sits within Customer Engineering, the technical arm of Mixpanel's Customer organization. Our sharpest focus is the digital-only segment: thousands of companies with no proactive account coverage. Some have technical resources available to them, but that support is entirely reactive. It answers the ticket and solves the problem in front of it. Nobody is watching for the customer who implemented and then never built a report, or the account whose usage has been sliding for a month. Our job is to be proactive,, and everything we build should be as automated as possible, without a human initiating it. Our programs run across the full customer base and are not one-size-fits-all. We build flows that branch and adapt by segment, tuning the content, timing, and channel for who's receiving them. An onboarding flow for a digital-only customer carries the whole experience; the version reaching an account with a dedicated team is tuned to complement what that team is already doing. Same underlying program, deliberately different execution, continuously optimized based on what each segment responds to. We're close to the data and to the technical reality of how customers implement and use Mixpanel. We're not guessing at what customers are doing; we can see it, and we build against it. This is a small, new team standing up a new function. The playbook isn't written yet; we're writing it together. About the Role As our Digital Adoption & Lifecycle Manager, you'll own the communications that drive adoption, retention, and expansion across Mixpanel's customer base, with our digital-only customers as the sharpest test of whether the programs work. You'll design lifecycle programs triggered by real behavior: a team that just implemented but hasn't built their first report, an account whose query volume dropped for three straight weeks, a power user hitting the edge of their current plan. Then you'll write the emails and in-product messages that move them forward. This is a builder's role, not a maintainer's role. You'll define the segmentation, write the copy, set up the triggers, instrument the measurement, and then argue with the data about what to change. It's also a deeply collaborative one. You'll work hand in hand with our Customer Success Digital Programs Manager, sharing a roadmap and dividing the work. You'll partner with Marketing on the overall email calendar so our lifecycle sends and their campaigns aren't competing for the same inbox. You'll support adoption initiatives coming out of Product, turning a launch into something customers actually try. And you'll take cues from customer-facing teams about what's landing and what isn't. Very little of this job happens alone. You'll also help define what agentic customer success looks like at Mixpanel. The scaled programs we build today are rules and triggers; the ones we build next will involve AI agents that can interpret a customer's situation, decide what that customer needs, and act. We're early here and we don't have the answers. We want someone who is already experimenting, who already has opinions about where agents help and where they break trust, and who wants to shape how this gets built. If you like clean handoffs and finished systems, this isn't it. If you want to build the thing from zero and own the number it moves, read on. Beauty operates at the intersection of fast-moving consumer trends and a complex, multi-brand global supply chain — and we are intentional about using technology to get ahead of it, not catch up to it. postings.text: Senior Product Safety and Compliance Engineer Location: Woodinville, WA OR New York City, NY ABOUT THE ROLE The Senior Product Safety and Compliance Engineer plays a lead technical role within Peloton’s global Technical Product Safety and Regulatory Compliance organization, ensuring connected fitness products meet the highest standards of safety, quality, and regulatory compliance throughout their lifecycle. Based in the Seattle area, this role works in day-to-day partnership with Product Development, Electrical, Mechanical, Software, and Quality engineering teams from early concept through post-launch support. The Senior Engineer brings deep expertise in structured problem-solving, leading complex 8D investigations, and driving preventive, systemic corrective action across the product portfolio to prevent recurrence. Additionally, this role leverages advanced data management and analysis to track trends, proactively surface emerging risks, and execute triage workflows for executive safety escalations. This position reports to the Sr. Director, Technical Product Safety & Regulatory Compliance. YOUR IMPACT AT PELOTON Lead Safety Investigations: Serve as the senior technical resource for complex product safety investigations, executing 8D methodologies, root-cause analysis, and sustainable CAPA workflows across the portfolio. Executive Escalation & Triage: Partner with cross-functional teams to create, maintain, and execute an expedited triage and response process for executive and member-facing safety escalations. Lifecycle Risk Mitigation: Engage with hardware and software product development teams from early concept through running production changes to identify design constraints and mitigate safety risks. Design & Risk Reviews: Review and approve product construction safety reviews, hazard analyses (FMEA, FTA), and engineering changes prior to release. Data-Driven Analytics: Build and maintain data tools and dashboards (SQL, Tableau) to analyze safety database trends, track compliance metrics, and surface emerging product robustness risks. Global Team Alignment: Partner closely with Taiwan-based engineering teams to ensure consistent safety and compliance standards across regional component and OEM/ODM suppliers. Certification Architecture: Develop formal certification and pre-compliance test plans, serving as the lead technical resource (remote and on-site) for product certifications at third-party test houses (UL, TÜV, Intertek). Standards & SOP Development: Create and update safety design documents, product communications, and new internal SOPs to embed compliance directly into the development workflow. Regulatory Intelligence: Perform continuous research on changing global regulations (CPSC, FCC, chemical, mechanical) and communicate actionable insights to internal stakeholders. Technical Mentorship: Provide guidance, technical direction, and structured problem-solving mentorship across the broader Product Safety and Quality engineering team. YOU BRING TO PELOTON Education: Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering or Mechanical Engineering. Experience: 6+ years of specialized experience in product safety, regulatory compliance, or quality engineering. Problem Solving: Master-level expertise in structured root-cause methodologies (8D, 5-Why, Ishikawa/Fishbone) with a proven record of leading complex technical investigations. Global Certifications: Demonstrated experience driving global product certifications through third-party laboratories like TÜV, Intertek, UL, and CSA. Technical Standards: Deep working knowledge of international mechanical and electrical safety standards (e.g., IEC 60335, IEC 62368-1, ASTM, EN 957/ISO 20957). Data Tools: Strong proficiency using data management and analytics software (Looker, SQL, Excel, Power BI, or Tableau) to interpret field telemetry and track metrics. Risk Methodologies: Thorough understanding of Design for Safety principles, product construction reviews, and hazard analysis

postings.title: Manager, Data Analytics, Performance Creative
postings.text: ABOUT THE ROLE Peloton is seeking a Manager, Global Performance Creative Analytics & Experimentation to help shape how creative drives subscriber growth across global performance and consideration channels. Reporting to the Director of Marketing Measurement Strategy, this role sits at the critical intersection of Data Science and Performance Creative, partnering closely with stakeholders across the global Marketing organization. The ideal candidate is a unique hybrid: an analytically rigorous professional who inherently understands creative DNA—someone who knows how to design clean testing frameworks while speaking the fluid language of creative production. Rather than analyzing performance as a static output, this individual will interrogate granular creative metadata (dissecting formats, messaging angles, visual hooks, and narrative structures) to deduce deep historical learnings. Serving as the team's institutional memory for creative performance, you will translate data into context-rich, highly executional insights that actively guide future testing and fuel a continuous creative evolution. Success requires the ability to move beyond passive reporting to actively guide creative test structures, answer why creative assets perform, and influence future global production and media strategy through data-driven insights. YOUR DAILY IMPACT AT PELOTON Lead the development and execution of the yearly global performance creative learning agenda. Yearly agenda should uncover new business and brand opportunities, as well as opportunity analysis on complex topics like creative fatigue and creative composition to suggest net new, structured tests. Consult on messaging and visual hypotheses in Creative Strategy’s quarterly learning agenda based on performance analysis and insights Based on the yearly and quarterly learning agenda, partner with Media Analytics, Media, and Creative Strategy to establish prioritisation, the methodology, execution, and roadmap of global performance creative experimentation. Align creative testing with the media testing agenda Scope and execute customised creative incrementality tests in partnership with cross-functional teams. Beyond standard A/B and multivariate methodologies, you will architect future-ready measurement solutions, proactively integrating AI and advanced modeling to mitigate data limitations and platform volatility whilst driving scalable, actionable creative insights Develop, maintain, and scale a proprietary "Creative Composite Score" framework to evaluate creative health, combining platform delivery metrics, attention/retention signals, and downstream business efficiency Partner closely with internal data engineering teams and external agency partners to expand, enable, and enforce a granular creative metadata taxonomy (spanning strategy, concept, and message levels), transforming the creative library into a highly structured, analyzable dataset Explore, vet, and integrate emerging AI tools and platform-native capabilities to automate creative asset evaluation and predictive performance modeling Connect creative performance signals across paid channels, lifecycle email, and landing pages to identify which messaging angles resonate across the full funnel—not just the individual ad unit. Actively participate in the Analytics and marketing broader team meetings, contributing creative measurement standards and cross-team learning to the centralized analytics core Modernize and elevate, where applicable, existing reporting frameworks to deliver more impactful, data-driven narratives. Establish a consistent cadence for performance communication, democratising access to key insights across the organisation to drive cross-functional alignment and enable rapid, actionable decision-making Maintain deep expertise across platforms including Meta, TikTok, Google, YouTube, and Pinterest, translating auction dynamics, machine learning optimization, and delivery systems into actionable creative briefs

postings.title: Retail Technology Systems Engineer
postings.text: Retail Technology Systems Engineer Sweetgreen is on a mission to build healthy communities by connecting people to real food. We passionately believe that real food should be convenient and accessible to everyone. Every day in each sweetgreen, our 5,000 team members make food from scratch, using fresh ingredients and produce delivered that morning. And in our local communities, we’re committed to leaving people better than we found them. We’re in the business of feeding people, and we’re out to change what that means. Our teams are our most valuable ingredient - the heart of our company, the face of our brand, and what truly makes the sweetgreen experience special and unique. The Retail Technology Systems Engineer sits on the Retail Technology team and owns the configuration, stability, and security of the technology running in every sweetgreen restaurant, from POS and payments to kitchen displays, connected kitchen equipment, and Infinite Kitchen locations. This role delivers new capabilities through successful go-lives, serves as the technical escalation point for restaurant support teams, and contributes to the future state roadmap for our restaurant fleet. You will: Implement, upgrade, and support restaurant technology across the fleet, including PAR Brink POS, PAR Payment Services card readers, KDS, and connected kitchen equipment, for existing restaurants and new restaurant openings. Build and maintain standardized device images and configurations in Microsoft Intune for POS, kiosk, BOH, KDS, iPad, and time clock endpoints, and release patches, enhancements, and fixes across restaurants. Build integrations and automations between restaurant applications using REST APIs, Workato, PowerShell, and Python, with a focus on reducing repetitive operational work. Monitor restaurant system health, resolve incidents, identify recurring patterns, and serve as the escalation point for Tier 1 and Tier 2 support teams. Partner with Software Engineering, Security, Networking, Operations, Marketing, Digital, and vendor partners to evaluate new hardware and capabilities, manage vendor escalations, and ready the team for new product launches. Keep restaurant systems secure and PCI-compliant, and maintain clear documentation, runbooks, and SOPs for support teams and fellow engineers. postings.title: Senior Food Safety Manager
postings.text: sweetgreen is on a mission to build healthy communities by connecting people to real food. We passionately believe that real food should be convenient and accessible to everyone. Every day, in each of our restaurants, we are creating an environment where people can come together over a shared love of real food. The Senior Food Safety Manager is sweetgreen's technical authority on food safety and sets the standards that protect our customers in our restaurants. This role owns food safety strategy and program design across the full fleet, serves as the subject matter expert the restaurant teams turn to on complex and high-risk issues, and carries direct responsibility for food safety performance in the New York City Region. You will define how we measure and improve food safety, partner with senior operations and supply chain leaders on the initiatives that keep our standards ahead of the industry, and be the person our operators trust when something goes wrong in a restaurant. You will: Set food safety strategy, program standards, and priorities for sweetgreen, partnering with company leadership on major initiatives from concept through measurable results and using risk, audit, and regulatory data to focus effort and investment where it matters most. Serve as the technical authority for the Food Safety team, guiding regional partners on complex investigations, high-risk escalations, and consistent application of standards across the fleet. Own food safety performance for the NYC Region, partnering directly with operators to deliver world-class standards in the restaurants and maintain compliance with federal, state, and local regulatory requirements. Own the NYC Region's third-party audit and pest control programs, reviewing audit results, sanitation violations, customer complaints, temperature monitoring, and pest activity, and driving corrective action to completion with timely documentation. Build the systems the function runs on, including SOPs, training materials, crisis management protocols, and reporting that tracks food safety and quality performance, evaluates restaurant-level compliance, and surfaces risk early. Build and maintain relationships with local health departments, guiding operators through inspections, violations, and requests, and keeping sweetgreen current on changes in government regulation and industry best practice. Keep open lines with partners across the company to surface food safety and quality issues early and turn them into continuous improvement opportunities. Desired Traits: Deep technical expert with command of pathogens and microbes associated with food production, microbiological testing, HACCP, SOPs, and the government and industry regulations, codes, and standards that govern food safety and quality. Influential without authority, able to build credibility with operators and executives and move standards forward through expertise and relationships. Problem solver who leads with root cause analysis and continuous process improvement rather than one-time fixes. Data fluent, comfortable working in food safety management and reporting systems and turning audit, complaint, and monitoring data into a clear picture of where risk sits. Clear communicator who can move between a restaurant walkthrough and an executive readout without losing the thread. Trusted partner who builds strong working relationships with local health departments and across internal functions. Generous with knowledge, and motivated by coaching and raising the capability of others across the organization. Self-directed operator with high integrity who takes initiative and delivers with limited oversight. Comfortable with travel up to 75% of the time and energized by time in restaurants. Desired Experience: 10+ years in food safety or quality assurance, ideally in a multi-unit restaurant or QSR environment. Track record building and scaling food safety programs across a growing footprint. Direct experience owning third-party au

postings.title: Quality Engineer
postings.text: Build quality into every product and help shape the future of AI-powered software. As a quality engineer at Gallup, you'll help deliver software our clients can trust by partnering with product managers, software engineers, designers and fellow quality engineers to ensure quality in every stage of the software development life cycle. Rather than simply executing test cases, you'll apply systems thinking to identify risks, develop thoughtful validation strategies and help ensure every release delivers an exceptional customer experience. As Gallup continues to expand its AI-powered products, you'll also have opportunities to contribute to testing intelligent workflows and emerging AI capabilities. What You’ll Do Develop a deep understanding of product features, customer workflows, system interactions, APIs, data flows, integrations and technical dependencies to identify quality risks and determine the most effective validation strategy Collaborate within Gallup's Product Operating Model alongside product managers, software engineers, designers and fellow quality engineers to ensure quality in every stage of product development Design, execute and maintain manual and automated tests across user interfaces, APIs, integrations and end-to-end workflows Develop and maintain automated test suites using Playwright or comparable modern automation frameworks Perform exploratory, regression, smoke and end-to-end testing to uncover system risks and validate critical customer experiences Integrate automated tests into CI/CD pipelines to provide fast, reliable feedback throughout development Troubleshoot automation failures and partner with engineering teams to improve test stability, reliability and automation coverage Create and maintain test plans and traceability that reflect product intent, customer impact and overall validation strategy Support production validation and investigate customer-reported issues when needed Continuously improve quality engineering practices, automation capabilities and release confidence What Makes You Stand Out Systems thinking: You naturally connect product features, APIs, integrations and customer workflows to identify risks before they become production issues. Quality-first mindset: You view quality engineering as an integral part of software development and proactively build quality into products rather than testing only at the end. Automation expertise: You develop maintainable, scalable automated testing solutions that improve release confidence and accelerate delivery. Collaborative partnerships: You build strong relationships across Product, Engineering and Design teams, communicating effectively to solve complex problems and improve outcomes. Continuous learning: You embrace emerging technologies, modern testing approaches and AI-enabled engineering practices while continually expanding your technical expertise. What You Need Bachelor's degree in computer science, computer engineering, information systems or a related field, or equivalent professional experience required At least three years of experience in quality engineering, including both functional and automated testing, required Experience testing web applications and REST APIs required Experience developing automated tests using Playwright, Cypress, Selenium or comparable automation frameworks required Experience working within Agile software development teams required Familiarity with Git and CI/CD pipelines required Experience using test management platforms such as QMetry, Azure DevOps Test Plans or TestRail required Experience with TypeScript/JavaScript and/or Python preferred Experience with SQL and database validation preferred Experience with cloud platforms such as AWS or Azure preferred Experience with performance, security or data quality testing preferred Experience contributing to automation frameworks and reusable testing utilities preferred Experience testing AI-powered applications, chatbots, copilots or intelligent workflow

You will develop and maintain policy frameworks governing condominium and co-op project eligibility, non-warrantable condominium lending, project-level risk assessment, documentation requirements, exceptions, investor compliance, and escalation practices. You will serve as a strategic partner to Credit Risk, Credit Operations, Capital Markets, Product, Operations, Legal, Compliance, and Technology. The role will translate complex credit, regulatory, investor, and market requirements into clear policy, effective controls, scalable processes, and executable business rules. postings.title: Lead Analyst, Financial Crimes
postings.text: About the role Chime's Financial Crimes team protects millions of members from money laundering, fraud, and the organized networks that target consumer financial platforms. We work in a bank-partner model: we run detection and investigation, and we escalate unusual activity to our bank partners, who hold the filing obligation. That means our written work product is read by outside parties, and the quality bar is correspondingly high. This is a senior individual contributor role. You will set the standard for how financial crime work is done here rather than working a queue — defining what good looks like, raising the ceiling for the analysts you lead, and owning the hardest problems on the team end to end. In this role, you can expect to Operate with minimal direction on problems that arrive ambiguous, and you define the approach rather than waiting for one. Set the quality standard others calibrate to with defensible judgement calls. Move work across team boundaries without formal authority, and you are trusted to represent Financial Crimes to partners outside the function. Raise the ceiling of the people around you — through calibration, coaching, documentation, and the examples you set in your own casework. Improve the system, not just the case. Every hard investigation should leave behind something reusable: a control, a procedure, a detection change, or a documented typology. What you will own: Vendor Management. You will lead, and support, a team of analysts. Vendor team quality. You sample operations work, run calibration with partners, keep apprised of quality assurance trends, and hold quality and productivity expectations where they belong. Risk trend analysis. You understand AML and Fraud risks well enough to follow the pattern of unusual activity across accounts, devices, funding sources, counterparties, and behavioral patterns, and you can show the shape of a network in a way a non-investigator understands. Typology development. You document new and evolving schemes, make them teachable to the wider team, identify if opportunities in coverage are needed, and own the creation of coverage with partners as appropriate. Operational rollout of new coverage. When a new typology or scenario goes live, you design how it will be worked — routing, procedure, evidence standard, and quality checks — before the first alert lands. Procedures and documentation. You own the SOPs for your area and keep them in a state where a third party could read them cold and understand what we do and why. Audit and exam readiness. You prepare the operational side for internal audit, independent testing, and bank partner reviews, and you own remediation of findings assigned to operations through to closure. To thrive in this role, you have 7+ years in financial crime, fraud, or risk investigations at a bank, fintech, payments company, or comparable regulated environment. Working command of BSA, the USA PATRIOT Act, OFAC requirements, and unusual/suspicious activity reporting standards — enough to explain not just the rule but why it exists. Deep experience across the transaction monitoring alert lifecycle at real volume, including the operational tradeoffs that come with it. Real typology depth across both money laundering and fraud — mule and money movement networks, first-party fraud, synthetic and stolen identity, scams and social engineering, elder financial exploitation, etc. Hands-on involvement in scenario tuning or threshold work alongside data or risk partners, with an understanding of what changing a threshold actually costs. Experience overseeing vendor or outsourced investigation teams. Judgment under volume. You can distinguish the case that deserves forty hours from the one that deserves forty minutes. Comfort with sustained ambiguity. You will spend real time on hypotheses that do not pan out, and you need the judgment to know when to stop. ABOUT PRODUCTION ENGINEERING Production Engineering is Ramp's infrastructure ownership layer. We exist to make Ramp faster, more reliable, and more scalable — and we do that by being embedded in the problems, not adjacent to them. A few things that define how we operate: - One team, one company, one objective. There is no "infra team" and "product team" — there is Ramp. We share the company's goals as our own. When a product team struggles with reliability or scalability, that is our struggle. - If reliability or scalability is at risk, we own it. We don't wait to be invited, and we don't ask whose code it is. If a system is slow, if it breaks, if it won't scale — that's ours to lead, regardless of where it lives in the stack. - We go first, and we go fast. When the path isn't obvious, we don't wait for someone else to find it. We move with urgency, propose the solution, align the stakeholders, and stay in until it's done — not until our ticket is closed. - We lead the way. We find the next problem before it finds us. And when we solve it, we don't just fix it for ourselves — the patterns and standards we establish become the foundation the rest of Ramp builds on. That's not a side effect of the job; it's the job. - We stay calibrated. Speed means nothing if we're moving in the wrong direction. We regularly stop and ask honestly whether what we're working on is still the highest-leverage thing we could be doing — the discipline that makes sure our effort compounds toward what actually matters. You cannot build the future of finance on shaky infrastructure. OUR TEAMS Production Engineering is organized into teams — but we think about teams differently. Teams are mutable. We build them around what needs to be done, not around what we need to do given the teams we already have. The structure below reflects our current priorities; it will evolve as Ramp does. Right now, we operate across four areas: - Compute — the foundation everything runs on: container orchestration, networking, load balancing, edge infrastructure, and the deployment systems that get code from engineers' laptops to production reliably and at scale - Storage — databases, caching, object storage, and the data infrastructure that underpins everything - Workflows & Messaging — the systems that power Ramp's financial workflows and event-driven architecture - Internal Infrastructure — the platform that makes every builder at Ramp faster and more autonomous: observability, cost attribution, and CI/CD systems that give teams visibility into what they build and what it costs WHAT YOU'LL DO Production Engineers at Ramp are full software engineers who happen to specialize in infrastructure. You write production code, you own systems end-to-end, and you drive technical outcomes across the organization — not just within your team. When a product team struggles with reliability or scalability, that is our struggle. - If reliability or scalability is at risk, we own it. We don't wait to be invited, and we don't ask whose code it is. If a system is slow, if it breaks, if it won't scale — that's ours to lead, regardless of where it lives in the stack. - We go first, and we go fast. When the path isn't obvious, we don't wait for someone else to find it. We move with urgency, propose the solution, align the stakeholders, and stay in until it's done — not until our ticket is closed. - We lead the way. We find the next problem before it finds us. That's not a side effect of the job; it's the job. - We stay calibrated. Speed means nothing if we're moving in the wrong direction. postings.text: Solutions for Today’s Challenges. Vision for Tomorrow’s Opportunities. Join William Blair, the Premier Global Partnership. Lead and execute private capital transactions end-to-end, including growth equity raises, minority and majority recapitalisations, private placements and structured equity for growth-stage companies. Build and maintain relationships with the broader private capital investor universe (growth equity funds, crossover investors, family offices, sovereign and strategic capital). A genuine passion for technology, innovation and disruptive business models, with the curiosity to develop deep conviction across technology and technology-enabled sub-sectors. First-hand experience of modelling cap tables including waterfall analyses of complex preference rights. Detail oriented with deep analytical abilities. Superior mathematical, writing, verbal and computer skills. Ability to adapt to new tasks with little notice. Ability to manage the expectations of senior bankers while working on multiple projects

postings.title: Senior Product Designer
postings.text: Hi, we're Oscar. We're hiring a Senior Product Designer to join our Product Design team. Oscar is the first health insurance company built around a full stack technology platform and a relentless focus on serving our members. We started Oscar in 2012 to create the kind of health insurance company we would want for ourselves—one that behaves like a doctor in the family. About the role: Oscar’s Internal Tools design team creates the mission-critical products that power our insurance and care operations. These tools support teams across Clinical, Core Insurance, and Network as they manage complex workflows involving claims, risk adjustment, provider networks, clinical care, and other essential business functions. As a Senior Product Designer, you will help define and deliver clear, effective experiences across this ecosystem. You will work closely with product managers, engineers, researchers, data partners, clinicians, operational teams, and other designers to understand complex problems, identify opportunities, and take solutions from discovery through delivery. The work is operational, workflow-heavy, data-rich, and technically complex. It requires strong systems thinking, comfort with ambiguity, and the ability to connect decisions across users, workflows, and products. Your initial product area will be determined based on your experience, interests, and Oscar’s current needs. Oscar is building an AI-enabled design practice. You will use approved tools such as Claude and Codex to clarify problems, explore workflows, identify risks and edge cases, and create realistic prototypes earlier in the design process. You will bring validated directions into Figma for complete state coverage, design-system alignment, and production readiness. You will also help the broader team develop effective and responsible ways of working with AI. This role reports to a Product Design Director. Work Location: This position is based in our Marina Del Rey office, requiring a hybrid work schedule with 3 days of in-office work per week. Thursdays are a required in-office day for team meetings and events, while your other two office days are flexible to suit your schedule. #LI-Hybrid Pay Transparency: The base pay for this role is: $149,040.00 - $195,615.00 per year. You are also eligible for employee benefits, participation in Oscar's unlimited vacation program, company equity grants and annual performance bonuses. Responsibilities: Independently lead the design process for complex problems, balancing immediate delivery and polish with a coherent long-term direction. Develop a deep understanding of internal users, their goals, and the operational environments in which they work. Partner with Product and Engineering to define product direction, identify opportunities, establish measurable goals, and contribute to roadmaps. Map complex workflows and systems to identify pain points, dependencies, duplication, and opportunities for simplification. Lead design work from early discovery and concept development through detailed interaction design, implementation, and iteration. Use research, data, hypotheses, and experimentation to evaluate ideas and improve product direction. Create prototypes that help teams explore ideas, test assumptions, and build confidence in a proposed solution. Lead workshops, product-vision activities, and presentations when they help teams reach clarity. Use Claude and Codex to clarify user and business needs, explore possible approaches, and identify requirements, risks, and edge cases. Use Claude and Codex to build and test realistic interactions, workflows, and front-end prototypes. Apply strong design judgment to AI-generated output, refining its structure, behavior, accessibility, and visual quality. Partner with engineers to determine which prototypes, patterns, or components can be carried into production. Use Figma to ensure validated concepts have complete states, follow shared patterns, and are ready for implementation.

postings.title: Psychiatrist - 1099 Contractor - Camp Hill, Pennsylvania
postings.text: About Lyra Lyra Clinical Associates partners with Lyra Health, a leading provider of evidence-based mental health care, serving more than 20 million people globally in partnership with employers and more than 100 million through health plan and partner relationships. The company has delivered more than 15 million sessions of mental health care, published more than 35 peer-reviewed studies, and delivered unmatched outcomes in terms of access, clinical effectiveness, and cost efficiency. Lyra members have access to care in one day, and nine out of ten improve with the support of providers like you. Lyra is transforming access to life-changing mental health care through Lyra Empower, the only fully integrated, AI-powered platform combining the highest-quality care and technology solutions. You will be contracted by Lyra Clinical Associates. About the Opportunity Lyra’s provider network is composed of in-person and virtual therapists, physicians, and coaches across the US. With our advanced matching technology, supportive provider platform, and opportunities for training and clinical consultation, being part of our network is an incredible chance to do what you love (like patient care) with support for the things you don’t love (like self promotion and scheduling). We are looking for contract psychiatrists who are passionate about whole-person, whole family mental health care and working within a connected network to provide patients with easily accessible, culturally responsive, high-quality mental health care. As a contract psychiatrist, you’ll provide evidence-based treatment via live 60-minute video intake appointments and regular follow-up appointments. You'll conduct psychiatric evaluations and provide medication management. Lyra makes it easy to refer patients to evidence-based therapy and coaching services in tandem with your care. You will provide care to individuals from a multitude of different backgrounds and experiences, as well as those with varying needs and abilities. We strive to continue to meet their unique needs by delivering culturally-responsive care—an approach that is mindful of the impact of cultural background on each person’s care experience. Responsibilities:: Practice comprehensive mental health medication management via a 60-minute intake appointment and regular follow-up appointments Conduct mental health risk assessments, psychiatric medication evaluations, and longitudinal medication treatment Construct patient-centered treatment plans, document treatment recommendations, message patients, and prescribe and manage psychiatric medications Experience and commitment to providing, evidence-based medication treatment that follows clinical best practice guidelines (e.g., measurement based care, patient-centered care Requirements: : Board certified MD or DO in psychiatry Unrestricted state license Strong preference for clinicians with an active DEA license Must have office space with ability to see clients in Camp Hill Ability to provide care to patients with a full range of diagnoses, clinical complexity, and severity levels, with a preference for providers who offer in-person options Full-time resident of the United States Here are some of the advantages of joining the Lyra provider network: : Set your own schedule without a minimum hours requirement Focus less on the administrative burden of billing with Lyra’s paperless billing and quick payment turnaround Access to a custom-built calendar for new patients to connect seamlessly Access to experienced clinical consultations to get rapid support with your patients. Have peace of mind with Lyra’s 24/7 Care Navigation team for client crisis support We are an Equal Opportunity Employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy), national origin, age, disability, genetic information or any other category protected by law. By applying for this contract position, your data will be processed as per Workforce Privacy

postings.title: Medical Assistant (Dougherty County)
postings.text: Salary Range: $23-$27 per hour About Clover Health At Clover Health, our mission is simple but powerful: to improve every life by delivering care that is high-quality, accessible, and rooted in compassion and innovation. This is not a clinic churn. It's healthcare in the home, caring for medically complex Medicare members where their real-life barriers are visible. You see the medications on the table, the fall risks, the caregiver dynamics, the food insecurity, the missed follow-ups, and the small clinical changes that can become major health events if no one catches them early. About the Role This is a full-time, field-based role involving daily travel to conduct visits in members' homes. Candidates must reside in or near one of our covered service areas throughout Georgia. We're looking for Certified Medical Assistants who are passionate about delivering compassionate, high-quality care in patients' homes. In this role, you'll work alongside providers to support patients with complex healthcare needs while helping improve health outcomes through personalized, community-based care. This is a full-time, Monday through Friday position. New Grads and Uncertified MAs Welcome: We know great caregivers come from every stage of their careers. Whether you've just completed your Medical Assistant program or have hands-on experience but haven't yet earned certification, we want to hear from you. Our goal is simple: we make it easy for the business to do what’s right for Clover. Clover Health's Member Experience organization is the front door to Clover for our Medicare Advantage members. Through our Houston-based service team, we are replacing the transactional, transfer-you-around call center model that seniors have tolerated for decades with a relationship-based one: a dedicated advocate who knows the member, follows their care, and can actually resolve things. We've proven the model works, and we are now investing heavily in the technology — including frontier AI capabilities — that will let us scale it to our full membership. Our mission is to improve the lives of Medicare Advantage members by making every interaction with Clover feel personal, competent, and resolved. In this role, you'll work at the intersection of service operations, product delivery, and change management — sitting alongside the advocates, team leads, and supervisors who deliver our member experience every day. You'll be the person who: Continuously evaluates the Houston Floor Team’s enabling technologies to determine what is actually broken and how badly. Carries that to engineering with the context they need to fix it. Ensures the fix lands on the floor instead of quietly going unused. This is deliberately a proximity role, and much of the job is human rather than technical. A service floor absorbs change constantly — new tooling, new workflows, new AI capabilities — while the phones keep ringing. Whether any of it works depends on whether advocates understand it, trust it, and can get a fix when it breaks. That is what you own. When their tools are good, members get taken care of. When their tools are bad, members feel it on the phone that day. Your work sits directly on that line. As a Product Operations Manager, Member Experience, you will: Embed with the Houston service team, building the direct relationships with advocates, team leads, and supervisors that make honest feedback possible. Own the problem statement, its severity, and its timing. When something surfaces on the floor, you define what is actually broken, how much damage it is doing, and when it has to be fixed — grounded in observed impact on advocates and members rather than on who complained loudest. Make the triage call and defend it. Sort need-to-have from nice-to-have from backlog, and explain those decisions face to face to the supervisors and managers whose requests didn't make the cut. Your credibility depends on your consistency and on people understanding your reasoning even when they disagree with the outcome. Run change management for the floor. Pair every meaningful release with the training, floor-level communication, quick-reference materials, and supervisor enablement that determine whether advocates actually adopt it. A feature nobody uses hasn't shipped. Build the floor's capacity to iterate quickly, establishing the feedback loops, pilot cohorts, and advocate champions that let us put a change in front of real users, get structured signal back within days, and fold it into the next iteration. Close the loop, every time. Tell people what happened to the thing they raised — whether it shipped, got deprioritized, or is still open. Nothing kills frontline feedback faster than the sense that it disappears. Help shape how AI shows up in the member experience, informing where automation genuinely serves the member, where it must hand off to a person, and how an advocate stays in control of the interaction. postings.text: Position Summary The Physician Advisor (1099 Contractor) is a licensed physician responsible for conducting clinical discussions with treating providers regarding utilization management determinations. The physician applies Medicare/CMS requirements, applicable medical necessity criteria, health plan policies, and clinical judgment to determine the appropriate level of care and/or medical necessity of requested services. The role supports timely, consistent, evidence-based utilization management while providing treating physicians an opportunity to discuss relevant clinical information before or following an adverse determination, as applicable. Key Responsibilities Conduct scheduled and ad hoc peer-to-peer discussions with treating physicians and other qualified providers regarding inpatient, outpatient, post-acute, and other authorization requests. Review the member's clinical documentation, utilization management review, applicable criteria, and rationale for the proposed or issued determination before the P2P discussion. Evaluate medical necessity and the appropriate level of care, including inpatient versus observation/outpatient status when applicable. Apply CMS Medicare Advantage requirements, the Two-Midnight benchmark, applicable NCDs/LCDs, MCG or other approved clinical criteria, and health plan policies as appropriate. Discuss the clinical rationale for determinations clearly, professionally, and collegially with treating providers. Consider additional clinical information presented during the P2P and determine whether it changes the medical necessity determination. Approve or overturn a proposed adverse determination when newly presented information supports coverage, within delegated authority and organizational policy. Escalate complex, high-risk, or unclear cases to the appropriate Medical Director or clinical leadership. Document P2P discussions accurately and contemporaneously, including the clinical information discussed, physician participants, outcome, and rationale. Complete P2P requests within established regulatory and organizational turnaround times. Identify recurring clinical, documentation, criteria, or provider-education opportunities and communicate trends to UM leadership. Collaborate with nurses, medical directors, appeals and grievances, provider engagement, and other operational teams as needed. Maintain confidentiality and comply with HIPAA, CMS, accreditation, and organizational requirements. Lead case review discussions on clinical JOCs Qualifications MD or DO from an accredited medical school. Current, unrestricted U.S. medical license. Board certification in an appropriate clinical specialty; Internal Medicine, Family Medicine, Emergency Medicine, or another specialty with broad medical experience preferred. Minimum of 5 years of clinical practice experience preferred. Experience with utilization management, medical necessity review, physician advisory services, payer medical review, or hospital case management strongly preferred. Experience with Medicare Advantage and CMS medical necessity/coverage requirements preferred. Familiarity with MCG, InterQual, CMS coverage policies, and the Two-Midnight rule preferred. Strong physician-to-physician communication skills and the ability to manage difficult or disputed clinical discussions professionally. Your Impact on our Mission Healthcare is complicated: people are anxious about their health, insurance coverage is obscure, and there’s uncertainty in finding the right type of care. Meanwhile, providers face thin margins, growing competition, and operational workflows that drown their staff in administrative burden. As a Principal UX Researcher, you'll immerse yourself deeply in understanding these problems, and own the research strategy for one of Zocdoc's two core user groups: the patients searching for care, or the practices delivering it. You'll report to the Director of Research and partner with Product, Design, Brand, Marketing, and Data Science leadership to proactively shape product strategy. You'll set the bar for high quality strategic quantitative and qualitative research that cuts across product teams and shapes the product roadmap. You'll identify unanswered research questions and unvalidated assumptions across the company, develop a clear POV on user needs, and use research insights to drive business objectives. Your work will span three connected areas: Define who we're building for, and what they're trying to get done. You'll use a mixed-methods toolset to map the jobs, needs, and mindsets of our users, helping product, marketing, and sales teams see which needs matter most and how they differ meaningfully across groups. Shape high-ambiguity problem spaces with qualitative and quantitative evidence. You'll lead research for zero-to-one opportunities where there's little precedent and limited data. You'll help teams define the problem, test the assumptions underneath a proposed solution, evaluate concepts at scale, and decide what is worth building before a roadmap hardens around an answer. Measure the user experience. Help product teams understand how well our products actually meet user needs. That means partnering with Data Science to define user-centered metrics, then standing up survey programs and tracking that make them measurable over time. postings.title: Senior Engineering Manager, Member Experience
postings.text: Omada Health is on a mission to bend the curve of chronic disease. Job Overview: We are hiring a Senior Engineering Manager to own a significant piece of Omada's Member-facing surface. You own what gets built, in what order, and how the people building it grow. A squad owns problems from prototype to production, including the maintenance and the on-call rotation for what it ships. At this level you own more than one, which means the hardest calls you make are the ones about where capacity goes when two good things want it at the same time. You stay technical. You are in the codebase and in the same agent workflows your builders use, close enough to review architecture, catch a weak design, and be useful in an incident. Where you manage directly, you ship production work off the critical path. Where you manage through someone else, that person's growth is your work product. You partner with Product Strategists who spend their time in front of members, coaches, and stakeholders, and who prototype to test ideas quickly. They own what gets built and why. You own whether it can be delivered, at what cost, and by when, and you are senior enough that your answer shapes the roadmap rather than just responding to it. About you: You are comfortable being accountable for what your squads ship. You still write code, and you want to. This role ships production work off the critical path, in the same codebase and the same agent workflows as your squads, so you feel the friction your people feel first-hand. You have a point of view on where AI-assisted development helps and where it creates rework, and it comes from changing how a real team works, not from reading about it. You have done the engineering manager job well enough that you can teach it. Whether or not you have carried the title of manager-of-managers, you have grown someone into leading, and you know the difference between doing the work for them and raising their ceiling. Your first team is your peer group, not your reports. When something is slowing down the engineering org and it is nobody's job, you have a track record of picking it up, getting the right people in the room, and finishing it. What you'll be doing: Own delivery across your squads. Sprint shaping, prioritization, backlog grooming, and estimation. Make the calls, write them down, and be accountable for them. When two squads want the same thing at the same time, you are the one who decides. Own cycle time. Yours to improve, not at the expense of quality, and yours to explain when it changes, including why one of your squads is slower than the other. Stay technical. On squads you manage directly, you ship production work every sprint, off the critical path, in the same agent workflows your builders use. On squads that run through a manager, you stay close enough to review architecture, catch a weak design, and be useful in an incident. Either way, you can teach someone to navigate the system, not just navigate it yourself. Partner with your Product Strategist. They own what the squad builds; you hold the line between their scope and yours so the squad never has two people answering the same question differently. Grow a manager. If an EM reports to you, their growth is your work product. Their squad's health is the evidence. Plan the team you need next year, not just this quarter. Headcount, skill mix, and the onboarding path that gets a new builder productive in an agent-heavy codebase in weeks rather than months. Set the AI standard past your own boundary. Write down what good looks like, teach it, and measure whether it stuck. Other squads should be able to use what you built without you in the room. Take on the problem that is nobody's. You will find things that slow down engineering broadly. Some of them you should pick up, organize, and close out with your peers. As a Product + Design Strategist, you will operate at a senior IC level: leading the highest-leverage, most ambiguous scopes of work at Omada and setting direction for a collection of related experiences rather than a single feature. You translate engineering’s increased pace into more of the right experiences launched for our customers and members, not just more output. Problem framing & requirements — turning a vague ask into a scoped, buildable piece of work. User journey mapping — diagnosing end-to-end friction and drop-off with empathy. Research study design & execution — running interviews, surveys, and experiments to test assumptions. Data analysis (quant + qual) — pulling product performance data and synthesizing qualitative signal into a clear read of the problem. Competitive, inspiration, & analogous research — auditing adjacent products for pattern or gap insight. Metrics instrumentation — in partnership with data analytics, defining upfront what “solved” will actually look like. Direction setting — reconciling research, data, engineering, and business input into a clear point of view on what to pursue, and revisiting that call against real evidence once it's live. Synthesis & direction-setting — recommending which directions to pursue and which to drop. Prioritization & trade-offs — arbitrating competing product and stakeholder requests with transparent rationale. Quantitative and qualitative evaluation design & analysis — defining core questions and hypotheses, then translating results into insights and go/no-go decisions. Stop/start/continue investment decisions — revisiting prior bets against evidence of what's actually working. Vendor & partner evaluations — build vs. buy justifications. Vision casting — making the future state tangible and compelling enough that cross-functional partners, leadership, and members can see it and support it. Roadmap ownership & narrative — owning a multi-quarter roadmap that maps to corporate OKRs, key strategic initiatives, operational cadences, and commercial cycles. Executive communications & narratives — building the strategic story for budget and prioritization conversations. Product marketing & commercial partnerships — carrying the vision into go-to-market and partner contexts. Brings strong product taste, and can articulate what makes a health experience good in both strategic and tangible terms. Prototyping — building click-through and interactive prototypes to test and communicate ideas.
